blocks.content: Quiz: Which of the following accurately defines a binary tree?
Tap an option below to answer:
A tree data structure that can only have a maximum of two child nodes.
A binary tree is defined as a tree data structure with a maximum of two children for each parent.
A binary tree is defined as a tree data structure with a maximum of two children for each parent.
A linear data structure where each element points to the next one.
Binary trees are not a linear data structure; they are nonlinear.
Binary trees are not a linear data structure; they are nonlinear.
A data structure where each node has multiple parent nodes.
In a binary tree, each node has, at most, one parent and two child nodes.
In a binary tree, each node has, at most, one parent and two child nodes.
A tree where each node can have more than two children.
Binary trees restrict the number of children to a maximum of two per node.
Binary trees restrict the number of children to a maximum of two per node.
